key_insight: Magnetism controls ordering in Fe-rich Fe–Si alloys: D0₃ ordering dominates in the fully ordered ferromagnetic state, while B2 ordering is promoted in the high-temperature paramagnetic state.
engineering_relevance: Linking magnetic state to atomic ordering can help guide composition and thermal-processing choices for Fe–Si alloys whose magnetic and mechanical behavior depends on atomic arrangement.
method: Calculate effective cluster interactions using density functional theory.
Resolve how magnetic state, lattice expansion, and Si concentration affect interactions.
Use Monte Carlo simulations to predict temperature-dependent ordering in bcc alloys up to 20 at% Si.
evidence_signal: The simulated ordering evolution reproduces experimentally observed phase equilibria and short-range order characteristics, although the abstract reports no quantitative agreement metrics.
watch_item: The demonstrated scope is bcc Fe–Si alloys up to 20 at% Si; extrapolation to other compositions or structures requires validation.
paper_title: First-principles modeling of ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys
